items.description: Report does not state the concrete fallback value when no override exists (fallback to 1 vs defaulting to 0 meaning 1 baseToken cap); the applied cap magnitude cannot be bound numerically.
Report does not give a numeric definition of the cap limit value or its unit, so the applied cap is represented as a qualitative keyed-lookup correspondence rather than a numeric bound.
Report does not state who calls initMarket or any authorization qualifier; the applicability scope of the requirement is limited to the lookup-key correspondence.
Fallback value for a missing noCapLimit entry is described inconsistently (fallback to 1 vs defaulting to 0 meaning 1 baseToken cap); no numeric cap relation is formalized.
Report does not give a concrete numeric intended noCapLimit value nor the exact fallback value; the applied and intended cap values remain symbolic.
Report inconsistently describes the fallback (fallback to 1 vs defaulting to 0 meaning 1 baseToken cap); the exact incorrect value is not fixed.
Report does not state the concrete mechanism by which the wrong-key lookup causes a revert/DoS on initialization; only the potential DoS outcome is asserted.
Fallback noCapLimit value is described inconsistently (fallback to 1 vs defaulting to 0 meaning 1 baseToken cap).
